summary: Qatar Tourism says citizens of over 102 countries are eligible for free visa-free entry (formerly called visa on arrival), including the US, UK, EU states and much of Asia and Latin America, and that the remaining nationalities apply for a tourist visa through the official Hayya platform for QAR 100.

primarySources.name: Hayya — official Qatar entry and visa platform
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar

defaultSource.name: Visit Qatar (Qatar Tourism) — Visas: nationality checker and visa-free list

US.notes: Qatar Tourism's nationality checker says US citizens receive a visa valid for two years, or until the passport expires, allowing multiple entries with each stay up to 90 days; the passport must be valid for at least three months and a hotel booking confirmed. Hayya issues it as the Visa-Free for US Citizens (F1) for QAR 76. The US State Department says no visa is required for tourist stays under 90 days and that there is a USD 21 entry fee.

GB.notes: Visa-free. Qatar Tourism's nationality checker says citizens can enter visa-free with a passport valid for at least three months from the date of arrival and a confirmed hotel booking. The UK government's travel advice says that to stay longer than 30 days you must extend your visa waiver through the Ministry of Interior before it expires, or you may be fined. The Consulate General of Qatar in Hong Kong lists this nationality for visa-free arrival for 30 days.

source.name: Consulate General of the State of Qatar in Hong Kong — consular services: visa-free arrival for 30 days

conditionalWaivers.text: GCC residents can apply in advance on Hayya for the GCC Resident Visa (A2): QAR 100, single entry, up to 30 days, with a GCC residence permit valid for at least 3 months, travelling from their country of residence.

source.name: Hayya — frequently asked questions (GCC Resident Visa, A2)

fee.notes: Hayya states the A1 visa costs QAR 100, paid on final approval and non-refundable; confirmed accommodation in Qatar is required.

source.name: Hayya — frequently asked questions (e-visa fee, Tourist Visa A1)

fee.notes: Paid at the airport, according to Qatar Tourism's nationality checker. For some nationalities, Iran among them, the checker requires a visa-on-arrival-eligible hotel stay booked in advance on Discover Qatar.

source.name: Qatar Tourism — Visas: visa checker by nationality

fee.notes: Applied for online on Hayya by US citizens only; a return flight ticket and accommodation details are required, but no proof of booked accommodation. Adults apply separately; US citizens under 18 can be added as dependants. Hayya calls F1 multiple-entry in its F1 answers but lists it among single-entry visit types elsewhere in the same FAQ.

source.name: Hayya — frequently asked questions (Visa-Free for US Citizens, F1)

fee.notes: For holders of a GCC residence permit valid for at least 3 months, travelling to Qatar from their country of residence; a return flight ticket is required when travelling by air. Dependants under 18 without GCC residence need a separate Tourist Visa (A1) or Visa with ETA (A3).

source.name: Hayya — frequently asked questions (GCC Resident Visa, A2)

passportValidity.text: Visitors need a passport valid for at least 3 months from the date of arrival, whether they enter visa-free, with a visa on arrival or with a Hayya e-visa (A1, A2, A3 or A4). Hayya, which issues Qatar's e-visas, states the 3-month minimum for entry through Hayya, and Qatar Tourism gives the same minimum for visa-free entry.

source.name: Hayya — Frequently Asked Questions: requirements for entry into the State of Qatar

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Qatar travel advice (entry requirements)
conflict.states: 6 months from the date of arrival

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Qatar country information

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged nine months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: Not required for visits of up to 30 days, though Qatar recommends health insurance for all visitors and sells it on arrival. Visitors staying longer than 30 days must buy health insurance from a Ministry of Public Health-registered insurer before travelling; the standard premium is QAR 50 per person per month.

source.name: UK FCDO — Qatar entry requirements (mandatory health insurance)

conflict.name: Serbia Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Qatar travel advisory
conflict.states: all visitors must buy health insurance from a Qatar-approved company

onwardTicket.text: Hayya, Qatar's official entry and visa platform, lists a return flight ticket among the requirements for entry into Qatar through Hayya, together with the Hayya e-Visa, a passport valid for at least 3 months from arrival and proof of accommodation. No official source we could read states the rule for visitors entering without a visa.

source.name: Hayya Portal — FAQ: What are the requirements for entry into the State of Qatar through Hayya? (passport, accommodation, return flight ticket, Hayya e-Visa)

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a funds requirement or amount for visitors to Qatar.

source.name: Hayya Portal — FAQ: requirements for entry into Qatar through Hayya (passport, accommodation, return ticket, e-Visa; no proof of funds listed)

currencyLimits.text: Cash, cheques or precious metals and stones worth more than QAR 50,000 (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to customs.

notes: The UK FCDO says Qatar has zero tolerance for drug offences, even residual amounts, and that some medicines legal elsewhere are controlled or illegal in Qatar. To bring controlled or prescription medication, follow the Ministry of Public Health's steps, including carrying a prescription and a medical report in English or Arabic, issued within the last 6 months; the Ministry runs an online permit service.

The UK FCDO says it is illegal to import, sell or buy vapes and e-cigarette products, including liquids and electronic shisha pipes, whatever the quantity; customs may confiscate them, and using them can lead to arrest, a fine, prison or deportation.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are widely accepted in Qatar.

safety.text: Canada's travel advice says the crime rate is low. The UK says that since 8 July there have been strikes and retaliatory attacks by Iran in a number of locations across the region, that travellers should be prepared for possible flight cancellations and airspace closures, and that they should stay away from areas around security or military facilities.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says high humidity and severe heat occur from June to September, advises carrying a sufficient water supply, and says dehydration and heatstroke can be fatal.

The UK FCDO says only licensed hotels, restaurants and bars can sell alcohol, the legal drinking age is 21, and drinking or being drunk in public is illegal. There is zero tolerance for drink-driving: any amount of alcohol can mean one month to 3 years in prison or a fine of QAR 10,000–50,000, and deportation.

The UK FCDO says to dress modestly in public, including while driving — men and women should cover their shoulders and knees — and that the dress code is strictly enforced in government buildings, healthcare facilities and banks, where you may be refused entry.
Qatar's e-visas, including the Tourist Visa (A1) and the GCC Resident Visa (A2), are applied for on the official Hayya platform, at hayya.qa or in the Hayya to Qatar app.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Qatar?
faq.answer: Qatar Tourism's nationality checker says US citizens receive a visa valid for two years, or until the passport expires, allowing multiple entries with each stay up to 90 days. Hayya issues it as the Visa-Free for US Citizens (F1) for QAR 76. The US State Department says no visa is required for tourist stays under 90 days and that there is a USD 21 entry fee.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Qatar?
faq.answer: Qatar Tourism's nationality checker says EU citizens can enter visa-free with a passport valid for at least three months from the date of arrival. The Consulate General of Qatar in Hong Kong lists every EU member state except Ireland for visa-free arrival with a maximum stay of 90 days in total, in one trip or several, within a waiver valid for 180 days that cannot be extended. Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs says Irish citizens can get a free 30-day visa waiver on arrival.

faq.question: What is Hayya and do I need it to enter Qatar?
faq.answer: Hayya (hayya.qa) is Qatar's official e-visa platform. Visa-free nationalities can arrive with their passport (Qatar Tourism says Thai, Ukrainian and Pakistani citizens must first book accommodation through Discover Qatar), while nationalities that need a visa apply for the Hayya A1 tourist visa there — QAR 100, with confirmed accommodation required.

faq.question: Can tourists drink alcohol in Qatar?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in licensed venues: the UK FCDO says only licensed hotels, restaurants and bars can sell alcohol and the legal drinking age is 21. Drinking or being drunk in public is illegal and can bring up to 6 months in prison or a fine of up to QAR 3,000, and there is zero tolerance for drink-driving.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Qatar?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says British visitors who need to stay longer than 30 days must extend their visa waiver through the Ministry of Interior before it expires, or they may be fined. No official source we could read states the length of the extension.
